narrative: Material PL1__MCCF3FA4 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=43.8%) with a statistically significant upward trend over the observation window (Mar 2025 – Mar 2026) and a mean daily demand of ~5,669 units. Lead times are short on average (1.37 days) but highly volatile (CV=68%), making lead-time variance the dominant contributor (76.8%) to the required safety buffer. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with safety stock of 9,946 units and EOQ-derived order quantity of 6,066 units achieves the 95% service level while remaining within the 20,624-unit storage cap and reducing annual inventory costs by over 96% versus the current zero-safety-stock SAP configuration.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock is 0 — material is fully exposed to stockout risk at current settings.
Lead time CV of 68% indicates highly volatile supplier performance; recommend supplier SLA review.
Upward demand trend detected — policy parameters should be reviewed quarterly.
Storage utilisation at 77.6% of capacity (16,012 / 20,624 units peak) — adequate but monitor.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With near-continuous non-zero demand (98.5% non-zero days), moderate CV (43.8%), and a short but volatile lead time, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy minimises total cost by triggering a fixed EOQ replenishment whenever stock falls to the reorder point. This is preferable to periodic-review for a high-velocity material where delay costs are significant.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 20,624 units is not binding: peak inventory (SS=9,946 + OQ=6,066 = 16,012) uses 77.6% of capacity. No capacity-driven reduction was necessary. However, if safety stock is increased (e.g. due to demand growth or supplier deterioration), the remaining 4,612-unit headroom may constrain future policy upgrades.
